llm_reasoning: Working memory is primarily supported by the frontoparietal network, which includes the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), the inferior frontal gyrus (IFG), and the intraparietal sulcus (IPS). The anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and the supplementary motor area (SMA) are also involved in executive control aspects of working memory. The cerebellum, particularly Crus I and Crus II, has been implicated in the coordination and maintenance of working memory tasks. The default mode network (DMN) is typically deactivated during working memory tasks, but some regions like the precuneus and posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) can be involved in self-referential processing during working memory tasks.
